newsitem.title: MEXICO: GFBital seeks 675 mln peso bridge loan.
newsitem.headline: GFBital seeks 675 mln peso bridge loan.

text.p: Grupo Financiero Bital is canvassing foreign banks for a bridge loan of 675 million pesos as part of its efforts to raise 1.5 billion pesos of new capital for its bank, Banco Internacional, a company spokesman said on Thursday.

"We're negotiating a one-year bridge loan which we hope to sign by December," a spokesman for the banking group, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters. "The amount of the funding will be 675 million pesos."
He said the loan would count on the guarantee of the controlling shareholders.
"The credit will be backed by the controlling shareholder group, and if the shares are not publically placed, they will acquire them," he said.

Bital in June increased the sale of net loans to the Bank Insurance Fund (Fobaproa) by 3.0 billion pesos, as part of a government rescue scheme in which many Mexican banks have been bailed out. In turn, Bital pledged to raise 1.5 billion pesos in fresh capital.
The bridge loan, he said, would tide the bank over until it completes a planned equity issue in early 1997.
"We're working on many fronts (for the capitalization) and the credit will be paid with the funds of a (share) placement next year," the spokesman explained.
Other plans for raising capital, he said, include:
-- Issuing subordinated debt for an amount of between 360 million and 400 million pesos before year-end;
-- Sales of assets for around 175 million pesos;
-- Capitalization of the dividends of its warehousing unit, brokerage and bond firms for around 75 million pesos.
